articles.title: GPT-6.1 Sol
articles.content:
We’re introducingGPT-6.1 Sol, an upgrade to GPT-6 Sol that nearly matches GPT-6 Astra’s intelligence on agentic coding, computer use, and professional work at one-fifth of Astra’s standard input and output token prices. Cached input costs just$0.10 per million tokens—95% less than standard input pricing and 50% less than GPT-6 Sol’s cached input pricing—giving developers more room to build and run capable agents that reuse context across requests.

Our most intelligent model for the
best results.

Near-Astra intelligence for a fifth of the price.

Fast and efficient everyday work
at scale.

GPT-6.1 Sol offers a new balance of capability and cost for important everyday work. It delivers substantial improvements over GPT-6 Sol across complex professional tasks, from writing and debugging code to understanding documents and executing multi-step business workflows. On several of these evaluations, it approaches GPT-6 Astra’s performance at substantially lower cost.

OnDeepSWE v1.1, which evaluates complex software-engineering tasks in real codebases, GPT-6.1 Sol matches GPT-6 Astra at roughly one-fifth of the cost, while eclipsing GPT-6 Sol’s best score by 6.4 percentage points at a lower reasoning effort and cost.

InDeepSWE 1.1⁠⁠(opens in a new window), AI agents solve original, long-horizon software engineering tasks.

OnGDP.pdf, which measures how accurately models answer professional questions using complex PDF documents, including tables, charts, diagrams, and fine-print details, GPT-6.1 Sol scores higher than Opus 5.5 with fallbacks at less than half the cost per task across the tested reasoning settings. It also approaches GPT-6 Astra’s state-of-the-art performance at roughly one-fifth the cost per task.

InGDP.pdf⁠(opens in a new window), models must answer real-world prompts about complex PDFs pulled from professional workflows in finance, healthcare, legal, and seven other professional domains.

OnAutomationBench, which measures whether agents correctly complete multi-step business workflows, GPT-6.1 Sol scores 2.2 percentage points above Opus 5.5 at medium reasoning effort, at roughly a third of the cost. That score is also up 4.8 percentage points from GPT-6 Sol at the same setting.

InAutomationBench 1.0.6⁠⁠(opens in a new window), AI agents are tested on end-to-end workflows using 47 tools across sales, marketing, operations, support, finance, and HR. The datapoint for Claude Fable 5.1 understates its actual cost, as it omits the cost of fallbacks, which occurred on ~40% of tasks.

GPT-6.1 Sol also makes substantial progress on tasks that require interacting with computer applications. OnOSWorld 2.0’s offline set, which evaluates agents on demanding computer-use workflows, GPT-6.1 Sol outperforms GPT-6 Sol by seven percentage points at maximum reasoning effort at less than half the cost. It comes within 2.1 percentage points of Astra’s score at maximum reasoning effort at roughly one-seventh the cost per task.

InOSWorld 2.0⁠⁠(opens in a new window), AI agents attempt long-horizon computer-use workflows spanning everyday and professional tasks. We report the partial reward on the offline set from the v2026.08.08 release.

OnTerminal-Bench Science 0.1, which evaluates scientific workflows including data analysis, simulation, and theorem proving, GPT-6.1 Sol more than doubles GPT-6 Sol’s score at maximum reasoning effort at less than half the cost per task. At maximum effort, GPT-6.1 Sol costs $5.47 per task on average, compared with $23.21 for Opus 5.5 and $23.80 for Astra, delivering substantial scientific capability at over 75% lower cost than either model.

GPT-6 Astra still achieves the highest score among the models tested at 68.1%, and should be used for the most difficult scientific research tasks.

InTerminal-Bench Science 0.1⁠(opens in a new window), agents complete scientific research workflows using code and terminal tools, including analyzing data, running simulations, and fitting models.

GPT-6.1 Sol also improves factual accuracy on difficult prompts. Its largest factuality improvement over GPT-6 Sol comes at low reasoning effort, where it reduces the share of responses containing a factual error from 11.4% to 7.7%—a reduction of approximately 32%. Across the tested reasoning settings, its error rate remains within 1.9 percentage points of GPT-6 Astra’s, at less than one-fifth the cost per task.

This evaluation measures the share of answers containing at least one factual error on de-identified conversations where users flagged an earlier model’s error. These deliberately difficult prompts are not representative of typical usage.

We evaluate factuality on de-identified ChatGPT conversations where users had flagged a factual error from a prior model. These error-inducing conversations are not representative of typical usage, where factual errors are more rare.

GPT-6.1 Sol shows substantial improvements over GPT-6 Sol in our alignment evaluations, bringing it closer to GPT-6 Astra.

GPT-6.1 Sol is more transparent about its limitations and more reliable at respecting user intent and safety constraints. In challenging evaluations, it shows lower failure rates than GPT-6 Sol on transparency about broken search tools, respecting explicit restrictions, and avoiding unauthorized outcomes during agentic tasks. We observed no attempts to bypass an automated safety reviewer, matching GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 Sol. Full details can be found in theGPT-6.1 Sol system card addendum⁠(opens in a new window).

The evaluations below deliberately test challenging situations and do not measure failure rates in typical use.

GPT-6.1 Sol is available starting today to all Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex. GPT-6.1 Sol is not yet available in Chat. Developers can also access it through the OpenAI API as gpt-6.1-sol. Its standard API prices are $2 per million input tokens, $0.10 per million cached input tokens, and $10 per million output tokens. In the coming days, we’ll also offer GPT-6.1 SolUltrafast⁠, with up to 8x faster token generation compared to its standard speed in Codex.

Evaluations of GPT were performed in our research environment or via our API, which may provide slightly different output from production ChatGPT due to differences in the system prompts, tools available, efforts, etc. Evaluations of competitor models were taken from publicly available reports.

articles.title: GPT-6 Astra
articles.content:
GPT

Astra

Update on November 17, 2026:Learn about OpenAI's latest model:GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol⁠.

Update on September 29, 2026:Learn about OpenAI's latest model:GPT‑6 .1 Sol⁠.

Update on September 22, 2026:We are expanding our GPT‑6 family with GPT‑6 Sol and GPT‑6 Luna.Learn more.

We’re introducing GPT‑6 Astra, the world’s most intelligent and aligned model.

GPT‑6 Astra brings together years of research and big bets across pre-training, reinforcement learning, and alignment. Astra is state-of-the-art on computer use, browsing, software engineering, cybersecurity, science, and professional work. Astra saturates FrontierMath Tier 4 with a 98% score, having already helpedsolve long-standing open problems⁠in mathematics. Astra also saturates ARC-AGI-3 with a 99.9% score and ExploitBench with a 100% score. It also sets a new frontier on computer and browser use, handling the most demanding professional work with unmatched speed, accuracy, and judgment.

GPT‑6 Astra is rolling out today to a limited set of organizations and over the coming days will become available to all ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users, as well as through the OpenAI API, Microsoft Azure, and AWS Bedrock.

Astra is our most aligned model, with substantial improvements in understanding user intent and model behavior—you can delegate tasks with greater confidence in Astra’s judgment. As one way that we test  this, we built a new evaluation informed by the Hugging Face incident that evaluates whether a model facing a difficult or impossible task will go beyond its intended scope. Compared to GPT‑5.6 Sol, which without production safeguards went beyond the authorized target 48% of the time, GPT‑6 Astra did this in 0% of cases.

GPT‑6 Astra marks a new frontier in the speed, accuracy, and safety of computer use. It can take care of tedious tasks like filling out online forms, updating customer records in a CRM, and organizing your calendar. It can conduct online research and draft summaries in your email or in your document editor. It can analyze scientific data, generate plots, create a website, and run frontend QA checks to make sure all the features on that site work. It can help you autonomously install and test software, and troubleshoot problems you see on screen. These improvements are also reflected in our state-of-the-art evaluation results.

These improvements also result in significant efficiency gains in real knowledge-work tasks. In latency simulations on OSWorld 2.0, Astra achieves higher computer-use performance in about 47% less time per task than GPT‑5.6 Sol, scoring 72.6% at roughly 40 minutes per task, compared with 65.7% at roughly 75 minutes.3

GPT‑6 Astra’s computer-use capabilities can be seen in outputs across domains, including game development, electrical engineering, and everyday knowledge work:

Alongside Astra, we are also updating the Codex harness to significantly improve the speed of computer use. Combined with Astra’s efficiency, this translates to a 1.9x faster task completion compared to the current GPT‑5.6 Sol experience, on the Mind2Web benchmark. The model’s improvements on speed mean it can take on many time-consuming life tasks for you, faster than you can.4

GPT‑6 Astra pairs advances in computer use with targeted training for professional environments, to help tackle complex work tasks. It combines the intelligence required for complex problems with the ability to carry out multistep workflows and produce polished documents, spreadsheets, and presentations.

GPT‑6 Astra is our best model for adhering to existing templates and producing slides that are well laid out and succinctly convey key points with a structured narrative. It creates clear, well-structured documents, presentations, spreadsheets, and analyses that follow your templates and match your writing and visual style. Astra is also trained to specifically pull only the context that matters into outputs, instead of repeating information unnecessary for the work at hand. All this means it can output more immediately usable artifacts that match your business context and standards.

GPT‑6Astra also brings stronger visual judgment to the websites, games, applications, and renderings it builds. WithSites⁠(opens in a new window)in ChatGPT, Astra can create, host, and share websites, web apps, and games directly from a prompt.

When instructions leave room for interpretation, GPT‑6 Astra is better than previous models at making the right call. It uses context to fill in routine gaps and asks focused questions when the answer could change the outcome. In Codex, it can ask asynchronously while continuing work that doesn’t depend on your reply. If you don’t respond, it proceeds with sensible assumptions where appropriate, but waits for your input on consequential decisions.

The examples below show how Astra collaborates on everyday tasks where missing information can materially change the answer.

Astra is also better at staying oriented as a task evolves. Earlier models sometimes treated steering messages as a new goal, losing track of the original request or earlier constraints. Astra incorporates new requirements, changes course when asked, and answers side questions without dropping the broader task.

GPT‑6Astra is the best model for software engineering to date.

With Astra, we’re introducing a new way for Codex to preserve and retrieve context when the context window fills. Historically, models have used compaction to summarize work during long sessions, such as when debugging complex issues or tackling large refactors. Each compaction can leave out details about why a fix failed or how a component behaves. In Codex, Astra can keep notes across context windows, preserving accumulated details without repeatedly compressing them into a single summary. Earlier context windows remain searchable, so Astra can find requirements or test results from previous messages and tool outputs—even if that information wasn’t captured in its notes. You can enable this experimental feature in yourCodex config.toml,⁠(opens in a new window)and it will become the default for Astra in the coming weeks.

GPT‑6 Astra is a major advance for scientific discovery, mathematics, and health. Today, we’re sharing two further results on the gaps between prime numbers.9,10

Astra also sets new records across a suite of math and scienceevaluations.

Astra can help with the practical work behind scientific discovery. By combining scientific reasoning with computer use, it can work directly in specialized software to inspect data and explore results, helping researchers assess the evidence and decide what to investigate next.

As we discussed in oursafety update⁠, Astra is a significant jump in cyber capabilities and meets theCritical thresholdin cybersecurity under ourPreparedness Framework. Its ability to identify and develop zero-day exploits can help defenders find and patch weaknesses, but it also creates a need for stronger safeguards. To understand how far these capabilities extend, we ran Astra on internal and third-party expert evaluations.

We first tested the model without production safeguards on ExploitBench and ExploitGym, which evaluate whether models can turn known software vulnerabilities into working exploits. On ExploitBench, Astra achieved a perfect score of 100%, compared with 78.5% for GPT‑5.6 Sol, our previous frontier cyber-capable model. On ExploitGym, Astra reached a 42.4% success rate, compared with 30.3% for GPT‑5.6 Sol, while using substantially fewer output tokens.13

Given concerns that exposure to historical software vulnerabilities may have affected benchmark results, we also evaluated Astra on two novel benchmarks. For one, we built an internal “ExploitBench (June–August 2026)” evaluation to test exploit development using vulnerabilities from the previous three months.14Astra achieved substantially higher arbitrary code-execution rates than GPT‑5.6 Sol on this dataset while using far fewer output tokens. During the evaluation, Astra even discovered and used two previously unknown zero-day vulnerabilities. We are disclosing both vulnerabilities to their maintainers.

We also tested Astra on SRE-Bench15, a benchmark that measures whether models can reverse engineer software binaries to understand its core logic without access to raw source code. Astra solved 88.0% of tasks in a single attempt and 99.2% within four attempts, compared with 55.9% and 68.7% for GPT‑5.6 Sol, respectively.

Beyond benchmarks, expert-led assessments found that Astra, when run without production safeguards, could use previously unknown vulnerabilities to achieve arbitrary code execution in hardened browsers and create privilege-escalation exploits for hardened operating-systems.

As we discussed inThe Defender’s Window, frontier cyber capabilities can help defenders find weaknesses faster, but they also make those weaknesses easier to exploit, raising the urgency for defenders to adapt. With the version of Astra launching today, defenders can use it to complete tasks such as secure code review and patching.

However, Astra will refuse to comply with more advanced cybersecurity tasks such as creating proof-of-concept exploits for vulnerabilities. ThroughOpenAI Daybreak⁠, we plan to expand access and roll out less restrictive safeguards in the coming weeks. This will enable more defensive workflows, including vulnerability and proof-of-concept validation, malware analysis, and detection engineering.

We have also strengthened our protections against potential cyber misuse, building upon our safeguards stack for GPT‑5.6 Sol. These include stronger model robustness to better withstand potential jailbreaks and more context for our monitoring systems. We have continued rigorous internal and external testing, including automated evaluations with ourinternal red-teaming attackers. More details about our cyber safeguards and testingare available in the Astrasafety overview...

articles.title: Meet Thinking Machines Inkling 2 Mini: 26B Looped MoE Runs on a 32GB Mac
articles.content: Thinking Machines Lab has released Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weight looped transformer with 26.4B total parameters. The model reuses its middle layers 3 times per token instead of adding more weights. That keeps the checkpoint near 20GB, small enough for a 32GB Mac or 1 NVIDIA DGX Spark. For developers, Inkling 2 Mini is a local option for agentic coding, tool use and document work. It ships under Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face, with hosted inference and fine-tuning on Tinker. TL;DR Size: 26.4B total, 3.4B active (5.4B effective per token with looping), up to 1M-token context. Runs on: Apple silicon with 32GB+ memory, 1 NVIDIA DGX Spark, or GPUs with 32GB+ VRAM. GGUF builds via Unsloth and llama.cpp. Performance: 20.1 on the Artificial Analysis Index, tied with Qwen3.8-27B (self-reported). Best: 79.2% on SWE-bench Verified (bash only). Worst: 15.2% on HLE-Diamond and 50.0% on MultiChallenge. Bottom line: Best: strong agentic coding from a 20GB checkpoint. Worst: weaker knowledge recall and multi-turn instruction following. What is Inkling 2 Mini? Inkling 2 Mini is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model from Thinking Machines that loops its middle layers. It accepts text and images and returns text only. It follows Inkling 2 Small, a 594B-parameter model released on November 5. How does the looped transformer work? The model stores 24 layers, grouped into 4 blocks of 6. The first and last blocks run once. The 2 middle blocks run 3 times with shared weights. That gives 48 layer applications per token from 24 layers of weights. Each pass after the first receives a “message” from the previous pass. Thinking Machines carries it with Attention Residuals and a learned gate. Feed-forward layers use 128 experts, with 8 routed per token. Looping the middle layers gave a 1.51x to 1.91x compute-equivalent gain. Looping the last layers gave only 1.24x to 1.36x. The middle-loop variant won 27 of 28 evaluations. Looping costs training compute but saves inference. An unlooped baseline used 7.5% less training compute. It needed 140% more inference compute to match the looped model’s loss on 512k-token agentic traces. How was Inkling 2 Mini trained? Training began with 384 experts per layer, with 8 active per token. At midtraining, the team pruned two-thirds of them and kept the 128 most-used experts. A 1T-token distillation run from a larger internal Inkling model then healed the pruned model. Post-training used SFT, then RL over 2.2T tokens and 2,000 steps, plus on-policy distillation. Expert layers are trained and deployed in NVFP4. The last 4 layers use MXFP8. Thinking Machines says this removes quantization conversion loss. A research variant, TML-d24-varloop-research, trains with 1 to 5 passes. How does Inkling 2 Mini perform on benchmarks? All Inkling scores below are self-reported by Thinking Machines. Coding is the strongest area. Inkling 2 Mini scores 79.2% on SWE-bench Verified (bash only) and 77.9% on SWE-bench Pro v2 (Hard). It reaches 48.2% on DeepSWE v1.1, where Qwen’s own card lists Qwen3.8-27B at 42.2%. On Terminal Bench v2.1 it scores 71.6%, behind Qwen3.8-27B at 73.0%. articles.title: OpenAI Ships GPT-Live-1.1 for Voice Agents, Cuts Idle Cost to $0.02/Min
articles.content: OpenAI has made GPT-Live-1.1 available in its API under the model ID gpt-live-1.1. The GPT-Live-1.1 voice model is a full-duplex model for multilingual conversations. It can listen while it speaks. OpenAI team states that it speaks with more natural and consistent accents across languages and completes tasks more reliably. The release also adds standby, a cheaper billing state for idle sessions. For teams running voice agents, idle time on a call now costs less. You can check the deployment options and specs here through our GPULeaderboard.com chrome extension. TL;DR Size: Live sessions hold a 128,000-token default context window. Runs on: OpenAI’s cloud only, via v1/live/sessions. Clients connect over WebRTC or WebSocket. No open weights, no quantized variants. Performance: OpenAI claims better accents, transcription, letter and number handling, and task completion than GPT-Live-1. No scores published. Best: Standby bills idle WebRTC time at $0.02 per minute versus $0.05 active, a 60% lower rate. Worst: OpenAI published 0 benchmark scores for 1.1. Image, video and structured outputs are not supported. Bottom line: Best: cheaper always-on voice sessions. Worst: quality gains are self-reported with no numbers. What is GPT-Live-1.1? GPT-Live-1.1 is a full-duplex speech model from OpenAI that hears and speaks in 1 stream. It follows GPT-Live-1, which reached the API on September 10, 2026. As per the OpenAI forum announcement, it has powered ChatGPT Plus and Pro voice since October 15. Inputs and outputs are audio and text. Image and video are not supported. Streaming and function calling work. Structured outputs, fine-tuning and predicted outputs do not. How does GPT-Live-1.1 work? The GPT-Live family replaces the usual cascade of speech-to-text, an LLM and text-to-speech. OpenAI says the model reasons over incoming and outgoing audio together in a single model. It also handles turn detection and returns ASR transcripts natively. Deeper work is delegated. The voice model can hand reasoning and tool calls to a backend text model. OpenAI names GPT-6 Astra for complex issues and Luna for high-volume tasks. Third-party backends also work. The Live conversations guide sets delegation.type to client or responses. Responses mode uses OpenAI models. Client mode connects your own backend. Instructions can run up to 16,384 tokens. What changed from GPT-Live-1? OpenAI lists 4 improvement areas for 1.1: More natural and consistent accents across languages More accurate speech transcription Better handling of precise details like letters and numbers More reliable instruction following and task completion How does standby mode work? Standby pauses inference during silence while the WebRTC connection stays open. The guide documents 3 settings: session.wake_policy.type: set to speech, so inference waits for speech session.idle_timeout_s: a whole number from 5 to 60 seconds session.wake_policy.vad_threshold: optional, 0 to 1, default 0.5 After the timeout, the server emits session.paused. When the user speaks, session.resumed fires. The session ID and history are kept. OpenAI warns the first reply after a short utterance may be slower. Keep the microphone track active during standby. Standby works for both GPT-Live-1 and GPT-Live-1.1. How much does GPT-Live-1.1 cost? You switch an existing Live session by setting model to gpt-live-1.1. Changing the model requires a new session. Outbound SIP calling reached all organizations on November 2, so phone agents are supported. GPT-Live-1 and GPT-Live-1.1 have separate concurrent-session limits. articles.title: A Team of Researchers from Columbia and CertiK Introduce TensorLean for Formal Verification of GPU Kernels
articles.content: Researchers from Columbia University and CertiK have introduced TensorLean, a framework for formal verification of GPU kernels at the PTX level. TensorLean is a Lean-based verifier that proves compiled kernels match a tensor-level math spec. The research team checked 149 kernel instances, including every kernel of FlashAttention-2, -3 and -4 plus DeepGEMM. It proved 83 correct. The remaining 66 led to 38 correctness bugs. TL;DR Size: 1.8K-line PTX parser. Specs total 10,278 lines against 151,285 lines of kernel source, a ratio near 15:1. Runs on: A 16-core workstation. It checks PTX compiled for A100, H100 and B200 kernels. Performance: 83 of 149 kernel instances proved correct, 38 bugs found across 6 projects. Best: Caught a FlashAttention-4 data race that never appeared in 17,760 test runs. What is TensorLean? TensorLean is a formal verification framework for GPU kernels at the PTX level. It starts from unmodified source code. A developer writes a tensor-level spec in Lean. TensorLean then proves 4 properties: no data races, termination, correct output within tolerance, and untouched memory elsewhere. How does TensorLean verify a GPU kernel? Specs build on Lean’s Mathlib. Tensor operators follow PyTorch names, so @ means torch.matmul. Each spec has 5 parts: spec_math, spec_mut, spec_layout, spec_tol and requires. The math stays separate from the memory layout. The pipeline runs in 7 steps: Start from unmodified source. Write the tensor-level spec. Compile to PTX and load a PTX semantics. Build a happens-before graph to check races and termination. Symbolically execute to get final memory, identical across schedules. Lower the spec to PTX-memory level. Discharge proofs with Lean’s kernel, Z3 and cvc5. Which techniques make it scale? Concurrency to sequential: Race-freedom proofs on the happens-before graph cover all CTAs, threads and loop iterations symbolically. Loop invariants over semirings: Closed forms for tiled, accumulating loops, such as online softmax, need 1 SMT query per loop. Tolerance proofs: Algebraic error is proved zero. Round-off error is bounded separately, then combined. Assertions as hints: Developers add tensorlean_assert in source. Each is proved once, then reused. What bugs did TensorLean find? The GitHub README lists 38 bugs, all reported upstream. FlashAttention accounts for 23. Liger Kernel has 7, TileOPs 3, TileLang 2, DeepGEMM 2 and Triton 1. By category, the site reports 19 memory access errors and 13 numerical bugs. It also counts 7 data races, 5 uninitialized memory reads and 5 undefined behaviors. There are 3 algorithm errors, 2 miscompilations and 1 deadlock. One bug can sit in several categories. Of 102 FlashAttention instances, 56 passed all 4 properties. The other 46 each failed a proof goal on a source bug. & How does it compare with other GPU kernel verifiers? TensorLean says equivalence checkers unroll loops for one concrete setup at a time. It uses symbolic parameters instead. Key Takeaways TensorLean proves GPU kernels correct at the PTX level using Lean, Z3 and cvc5. 83 of 149 kernel instances proved correct; 38 bugs found. 23 bugs sit in FlashAttention-2, -3 and -4. articles.title: Baseten Releases Bison-1 and Groundhog-1, Topping Decision Model Index
articles.content: Baseten has released bison-1 and groundhog-1, 2 open-weight decision models built on Google’s Gemma 4. Decision models do not write text. They return calibrated probabilities for yes/no, choice and score questions. The Baseten bison-1 decision model scores 76 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1. That ranks #1 of 19. Both models raise context from 16k to 128k tokens and accept images. For routing, triage and guardrail pipelines, that means full policies and histories in one call. TL;DR Size: bison-1 is 31B dense. groundhog-1 is a 26B MoE with about 4B active. Both take 128k tokens (131,072). Runs on: Baseten Model APIs, plus open BF16 weights on Hugging Face. No inference GPU or quantized builds are listed. BF16 weights alone are about 62 GB (bison-1) and 52 GB (groundhog-1), by our arithmetic. Performance: bison-1 scores 76 on AA Decision Index v2.1, 1 point above Liquid AI’s d1.2-ultra (75). Best: When2Call, 98 (rank #1). Worst: AA-Omniscience-Decision v1.1, 60 (rank #11). Bottom line: Best: top-ranked, best-calibrated decisions (Brier 0.14) over 128k tokens at $0.10 per 1M input tokens. Worst: groundhog-1 has no official index score yet, and every number is self-reported. What are bison-1 and groundhog-1? bison-1 is a 31B decision model from Baseten that post-trains Gemma 4 31B to return calibrated probabilities. groundhog-1 is the cheaper sibling. It fine-tunes Gemma 4 26B-A4B, a mixture-of-experts model with about 4B active parameters per token. Both join Baseten’s existing lineup: mammoth-1 (27B), elephant-1 (9B) and joey-1 (2B). Those 3 sit on Qwen backbones. The new pair is Baseten’s first on what it calls an American backbone. How does a decision model work? A request carries 1 state and any number of questions. The state is text, optionally with images. Each question has a type: noul (yes/no), choice (named options) or score (ordered levels). The model answers every question in a single prefill pass. It returns P(yes), or the chosen option with a probabilities field. No output tokens are generated. Baseten’s earlier launch post lists ticket triage, spam detection, jailbreak guardrails and LLM routing as target tasks. Requests longer than the trained limit are refused, not truncated. Pipelines that assume silent truncation will need a length check. Why is bison-1 better calibrated? Baseten credits two sources: the Gemma base and more “soft labels” in the training mix. Soft labels use probability targets instead of 1 fixed correct answer. The model learns to report uncertainty that tracks how often it is right. The result is a Brier score of 0.14, the lowest on the index. Baseten puts d1.2-ultra at 0.15. Lower is better. How does bison-1 score on benchmarks? On AA Decision Index v2.1, bison-1 scores 76. Liquid AI’s d1.2-ultra scores 75 and mammoth-1 scores 71. The index blends 6 evaluations, led by AA-Paperclip at 30%. The bison-1 model card breaks out each component: When2Call: 98 (#1) EvalSafe-O*NET-AA: 93 (#1) AA-Symmetry v1.1: 89 (#1) AA-Paperclip: 73 (#2) HLE-MultiChoice v1.1: 51 (#1) AA-Omniscience-Decision v1.1: 60 (#11) bison-1 ranks first on 4 of 6 components. Knowledge-heavy decisions are its weak spot. On long context, Baseten reports LongMemEval M (128k) of 84.8 for bison-1 and 77.4 for groundhog-1. LongMemEval S reads 87.1 and 79.3. groundhog-1 has no official index score yet. Baseten expects it to match mammoth-1. articles.summary: Baseten은 Gemma 4 기반 공개 가중치 의사결정 모델 bison-1과 groundhog-1을 출시했다고 보도됐다. 두 모델은 자유 형식 문장을 생성하기보다 예·아니요, 선택지, 점수 질문에 대한 보정된 확률을 반환하며, 이미지와 128K 토큰 문맥을 처리한다. bison-1은 제시된 Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1에서 76점으로 19개 모델 중 1위지만, 기사에서는 수치가 자체 보고됐고 groundhog-1의 공식 지수 점수는 없다고 명시했다. 긴 정책과 이력을 한 번에 읽어 라우팅·분류·가드레일 결정을 수행하는 용도에 적합한 설계다.

articles.title: Moving Generality from Model to Modeler: LLM Agents for PHM on a Deployment-Style Benchmark
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25252v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coding agents built on large language models (LLMs) now help develop many models published as general solutions. Should generality instead reside in the agent that builds a model for each new task? We examine this question in prognostics and health management (PHM), where every model must work on unseen equipment. Our deployment-style benchmark, NextUnit-Bench, covers 24 public datasets split into 58 folds that hold out units or operating conditions; each agent has two hours to deliver an executable predictor, then run on the hidden units. First, frontier agents outperform AutoML, which reaches less than half the best agent's score, and faithful implementations of published methods on four datasets, of which only 6 of 30 beat the strongest agent's own design; published accuracies, where reproducible, rest on the papers' own conventions, and a single convention, capping the remaining life of test engines, can halve the reported error. Second, the agents' advantage is a design made on each machine's data; once made, a plain-text plan of a few hundred words carries most of the gap between two frontier agents, and given a weaker agent's plan, the strongest agent falls to that agent's level, often to identical predictions. Before touching the data, however, it matters little whose plan an agent carries out, and domain toolkits appear to help neither: what sets the strongest apart is how much it learns from the data. Third, such designs reach only implementers that can execute them: given the strongest agent's designs, a locally deployable open-weight model delivers half as often, even when they are lightened, and scores no higher than without them. Generality, we argue, is not disappearing but moving, from the model to the modeler.
articles.summary: NextUnit-Bench 연구는 설비 예지보전 분야의 24개 공개 데이터셋을 58개 분할로 구성하고, 코딩 에이전트가 두 시간 안에 만든 예측기를 미관측 장비나 운전 조건에서 평가했다. 이 조건에서 AutoML의 점수는 최상위 에이전트의 절반에 못 미쳤으며, 성능 차이의 상당 부분은 데이터를 살펴본 뒤 작성한 수백 단어의 설계 계획으로 전달됐다. 반면 로컬 배포 가능한 공개 가중치 모델은 강한 에이전트의 설계를 받아도 구현 성공률이 낮아 같은 이점을 확보하지 못했다. 결과는 산업별 맞춤 모델 개발을 자동화할 가능성을 보여주지만, 설계 품질뿐 아니라 실행 능력과 배포를 모사한 평가 방식이 중요하다는 점도 드러낸다.

articles.title: Some Memories Must Fade: Persistence and Decay of User Memories in Model Parameters
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25235v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Parametric memory allows Large Language Models to internalize knowledge directly into their weights, offering a potentially powerful alternative to retrieval-based memory (RAG). However, existing approaches to parametric memory are difficult to deploy as they largely mirror the Continual Learning (CL) objective of retaining information indefinitely. This is neither sustainable nor sufficient for a memory system, which must govern knowledge across its lifecycle by retaining stable facts, reinforcing recurring observations, updating changed beliefs, and allowing transient information to fade. We propose a system for parametric memory management consisting of a memory substrate (handling information storage and forgetting) and a learned policy (what to remember, how deeply, and for how long). Our substrate is a fixed-capacity LoRA adapter that consists of k-hot rank combinations which store facts without catastrophic interference and maintain an independently controlled temporal decay, enabling outdated information to fade while long-term facts persist. On this substrate, we train a lightweight controller that governs each incoming user event to ensure the memory system reflects the user's true, updated belief state. To evaluate how memory systems manage user memory, we introduce a controlled dataset of long-horizon user trajectories with varying persistence of facts based on changing belief states and user-behavioral shifts, and probe queries that test recall while information is valid and abstention after it expires. Our policy learns to effectively manage user memory over its entire lifecycle, balancing recall and abstention to achieve 86% of oracle performance, unlike CL and RAG baselines that primarily default to one of the two behaviors. By providing the first system to manage memory directly in model weights, this work establishes a foundation for long-horizon parametric memory.
articles.summary: 연구진은 사용자 정보를 무기한 보존하기보다 유지·갱신·망각을 함께 관리하는 모델 가중치 기반 기억 시스템을 제안했다. 고정 용량 LoRA 어댑터의 k-hot 랭크 조합에 사실을 저장하고 독립적인 시간 감쇠를 적용하며, 경량 학습 제어기가 무엇을 얼마나 오래 기억할지 결정한다. 변화하는 사용자 상태를 모사한 통제 데이터셋에서 유효한 정보의 회상과 만료 정보에 대한 응답 유보를 균형 있게 수행해 오라클 성능의 86%를 달성했다고 보고했다. 장기 개인화 에이전트의 오래된 기억 문제를 다루는 접근이지만, 실제 사용자 환경에서의 효과는 추가 검증이 필요하다.

articles.title: Learning to Read Events for Exact State Tracking with Frozen Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25211v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long event streams require identifying each change and applying the changes in order. We train a selector on a frozen language model to read each transition. With API-only access, we ask the model to list the transitions. An external integer register composes them in order. A confidence rule can flag uncertain updates or retain several candidates. We study products of permutations of five items, a task that fixed-depth, log-precision transformers cannot solve on all input lengths under the standard conjecture that $\mathrm{TC}^0 \ne \mathrm{NC}^1$. On two-event windows, a 27B model answered 3 of 100 correctly without visible reasoning and 96 of 100 when it generated intermediate steps. A frozen 0.8B model with a trained selector read every event in 299 of 299 windows of 43,687 events each. The same package passed 298 of 299 new windows on a fresh machine, missing the target of 0.99 for the one-sided 95% lower confidence bound. A separate follow-up sized to allow one failure yielded 472 of 473. On 1,000-event room-swap documents, three of ten models solved all five documents by reasoning alone. All seven models tested both ways at this length solved all five with extraction and the register, with no chain of thought requested. With concurrent extraction, median wall-clock time fell from 136.1 to 10.4 s for Sonnet 5.5 and from 313.5 to 28.0 s for GPT-6.1 Sol. At fixed per-token rates, mean cost per document fell by 55% for Sonnet 5.5 and 44% for GPT-6.1 Sol. A regular expression with an executor also solved all 15 fixed-format documents. On 500 free-form issue-tracker comments, a separately adapted 4B reader identified the recorded value in 68.8% of cases, compared with 61.0% for a frequency baseline fitted on the same training projects.
articles.summary: 이 연구는 긴 사건열의 상태 추적을 언어모델의 전이 추출과 외부 정수 레지스터의 순차 실행으로 분리했다. 가중치를 고정한 소형 모델에 선택기를 학습시키거나 API 모델에 사건을 추출하게 해, 긴 중간 추론 없이 상태를 계산하는 방식이다. 1,000개 사건의 방 교환 문서에서는 두 방식을 모두 평가한 7개 모델이 추출·레지스터 방식으로 문서 5개를 모두 해결했고, 일부 모델은 병렬 추출로 시간과 비용도 줄였다. 다만 재현 시험 하나는 사전 설정한 신뢰하한 목표에 미달했으며, 자유 형식 이슈 댓글의 정확도는 68.8%여서 정형 과제의 높은 성능을 일반화하기는 어렵다.

articles.title: Watch Where You Linearize: Predicting and Correcting Model-Merging Interference
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25000v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Model merging combines separately fine-tuned models by adding their task vectors to a shared backbone. Interference is typically assessed only after constructing and evaluating a candidate merge, making coefficient search expensive. We show that a first-order directional derivative of task A's outputs along task B's vector can predict interference, but only when evaluated at the appropriate model.
  At the receiver model, this derivative forecasts nearby merges per task and per example, halves the accuracy error of a no-change baseline, and identifies most examples whose predictions flip. For full multi-task merges, a single evaluation is insufficient; two evaluations along the merge path are needed. At the shared pretrained backbone, however, the derivative is nearly orthogonal to realized changes in our vision experiments and only partly predictive in LoRA language-model pilots. Controls link this failure to displacement along the receiver's own task vector, not simply parameter distance; the mismatch appears within the first few dozen fine-tuning steps.
  Freezing receiver-local responses produces a surrogate affine in the merge coefficients. We use it to construct LR-Merge, a label-free correction that optimizes coefficients through convex teacher matching on unlabeled probes, without backpropagation through merged networks. LR-Merge improves all tested closed-form, isotropic, and sparsified base mergers, with gains generally increasing as more tasks are merged. Using pretrained rather than receiver-local responses instead degrades the base merge. LR-Merge matches exact teacher matching through a merged network, which takes roughly three times longer to converge and performs similarly at an equal compute budget. Once built, the surrogate answers new coefficient and task-subset queries in seconds.
articles.summary: 모델 병합 연구는 작업 벡터 간 간섭을 예측할 때 공통 사전학습 모델이 아니라 해당 작업에 미세조정된 수신 모델에서 방향 미분을 계산해야 한다고 보고했다. 이를 이용한 LR-Merge는 라벨 없는 입력에서 얻은 국소 반응으로 대리 모델을 만들고, 병합 모델을 통한 역전파 없이 볼록 최적화로 혼합 계수를 보정한다. 시험한 기본 병합 방법 전반에서 개선을 보였으며, 대리 모델을 구축한 뒤에는 새 계수나 작업 부분집합 질의에 수초 내 응답했다. 여러 특화 모델을 결합하는 탐색 비용을 줄일 수 있지만, 전체 다중 작업 병합에는 경로상의 두 차례 평가가 필요하고 언어모델 실험은 예비적 범위다.

articles.title: Separating Interpretability and Reconstruction in Sparse Autoencoders
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25165v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) are effective tools for mechanistic interpretability by decomposing neural representations into sparse and interpretable features. However, a single sparse representation in traditional SAEs is responsible for both reconstruction fidelity and interpretability, which are not guaranteed to align. To separate these objectives, we propose DualSAE, a modular framework that augments standard SAEs with a plug-in Residual Branch. A standard SAE serves as the Sparse Branch, learning a sparse code that contains the dominant semantics of the input. The added Residual Branch models the non-semantic information omitted by the Sparse Branch. We ensure that the contributions of the two branches towards the overall reconstruction have minimal overlap through a decorrelation loss. We also adopt a two-stage training strategy that first stabilizes sparse representation learning before coupling with the Residual Branch. Across diverse encoder-SAE configurations on two vision datasets and two language corpora, DualSAE achieves mean relative improvements of approximately 29% in reconstruction fidelity and 34% in interpretability (measured by monosemanticity score). Moreover, with more interpretable representations, DualSAE yields consistent performance gains in the downstream applications of topic modeling, hypothesis generation, and LLM steering. Qualitative analysis further suggests that the Sparse Branch indeed preserves dominant semantic content, whereas the Residual Branch captures non-semantic information to improve reconstruction fidelity.
articles.summary: DualSAE는 희소 오토인코더가 해석 가능성과 입력 재구성을 동시에 떠맡는 구조를 분리하기 위해 잔차 분기를 추가했다. 희소 분기는 지배적인 의미를, 잔차 분기는 누락된 비의미적 정보를 담당하도록 설계하고, 비상관 손실과 두 단계 학습으로 중복을 줄인다. 두 비전 데이터셋과 두 언어 코퍼스에서 재구성 충실도와 단일 의미성 기반 해석 가능성이 평균적으로 각각 약 29%, 34% 상대 개선됐다고 보고했다. 주제 모델링·가설 생성·LLM 조향에서도 개선을 보여 내부 표현 분석에 유용할 수 있지만, 해석 가능성의 향상은 사용한 측정 지표와 평가 범위 안에서 이해해야 한다.

articles.title: Game-Theoretic Data Allocation for Expert Specialization and Routing
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25167v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Can the allocation used to train experts also predict which expert will perform best on a prompt? Such a connection would make the intended division of labor inspectable before training and allow the allocation itself to guide inference. We introduce InflEns, a mixture of LoRA experts whose training weights and inference routes come from the same location game in a fixed prompt-trait space. Players choose positions to maximize their expected shares of the prompt distribution, without using expert losses. We utilize the game's kernel-general theoretical criterion for when co-located positions become locally unstable to separation. We evaluate InflEns on a corpus assembled from seven safety-related benchmarks, which demonstrates that the highest-share expert has the lowest held-out response negative log-likelihood (NLL) on approximately 90% of prompts across four kernels under a sharpened simplex representation, compared with approximately 15% after permuting allocations across prompts. We demonstrate that the method performs comparably to published learned gates without having to train an explicit gate on the experts. Because the router is fixed, we can trace harmful behavior to a single expert and retrain only that expert, which lowers HarmBench attack success from 0.51 to 0.02 while keeping instruction following. The game also gives us several controls over how the experts specialize, including the kernel choice and its parameters, the trait-space geometry, and the number of experts. Importantly, InflEns is a general framework that can be extended to any encoder and data distribution.
articles.summary: InflEns는 고정된 프롬프트 특성 공간의 위치 게임으로 LoRA 전문가들의 학습 데이터 배분과 추론 라우팅을 함께 정하는 프레임워크다. 안전 관련 7개 벤치마크로 구성한 코퍼스에서 특정 표현 설정을 적용했을 때, 가장 높은 배분 몫을 가진 전문가가 약 90%의 프롬프트에서 가장 낮은 응답 음의 로그우도를 보였다. 별도 학습 게이트 없이 비교 가능한 라우팅 성능을 보고했으며, 유해 행동과 연결된 전문가만 재학습해 HarmBench 공격 성공률을 0.51에서 0.02로 낮추면서 지시 이행을 유지했다. 전문가 분업을 사전에 살펴보고 국소적으로 수정할 수 있다는 장점이 있지만, 결과는 시험한 특성 공간과 데이터 구성에 의존한다.

articles.title: 최태원 회장, “AI 네이티브 대학, 설계부터 바꿔야”...韓日 기업·대학 공동 AI 인재 육성 제안
articles.content:
최태원 SK그룹 회장 겸 최종현학술원 이사장이 인공지능(AI)을 일상적인 환경으로 받아들이는 'AI 네이티브 사회'에 대응하기 위해 대학 교육체계를 근본적으로 재설계해야 한다고 강조했다. 특히 한국과 일본의 기업·대학이 공동으로 AI 인재를 육성하고, 양국의 인턴십과 일자리를 연계하는 협력 프로그램을 제안했다.

최종현학술원과 일본 도쿄대학교(University of Tokyo)는 지난 20일부터 21일까지 이틀간 일본 도쿄대 야스다 강당에서 '변혁적 기술로서의 AI: 인류, 지식, 그리고 문명'을 주제로 '도쿄포럼 2026(Tokyo Forum 2026)'을 개최했다.

2019년부터 매년 열린 도쿄포럼은 글로벌 현안을 논의하는 국제 학술행사다. 올해는 최 회장을 비롯해 앤 부베로 프랑스 정부 AI 특사, 이토 렌 사카나 AI 공동창업자 등 각국 전문가들이 참석해 AI가 사회와 지식체계, 인류 문명에 미칠 영향을 논의했다.

최 회장은 21일 비즈니스리더 세션에서 “AI 네이티브 사회는 AI를 단순히 활용하는 사회가 아니라, AI를 당연히 주어진 환경으로 받아들이는 사회”라며 “지금의 대학 체계를 비롯해 사회 전반을 다르게 설계해야 하는 만큼 새로운 거버넌스와 체계가 필요하다”고 말했다.

특히 “기존 교육과정을 조금 고치는 것만으로는 충분하지 않다”며 “AI 네이티브 대학은 완전히 다른 설계와 거버넌스를 갖춰야 한다”고 강조했다. AI 시대에 요구되는 교육은 지식을 전달하는 기존 방식에서 벗어나 학생들이 스스로 문제를 정의하고 해결 방법을 설계하는 방향으로 변화해야 한다는 설명이다.

최 회장은 “AI는 새로운 것이고 아무도 답을 갖고 있지 않기 때문에 집단지성을 모아 답을 찾아야 한다”며 교육 과정에서 직접 시스템을 설계하고 시행착오를 경험하는 일이 미래의 문제 해결 역량으로 이어질 수 있다고 설명했다.

기업의 인재 육성 사례로는 SK가 지난달 선보인 2년제 비학위 교육 프로그램 '아이젠(AIGEN)'을 소개했다. 아이젠은 참가자들이 팀 프로젝트를 수행하면서 다양한 분야의 문제를 해결하는 방식으로 운영된다. 최 회장은 “팀 프로젝트를 주고 스스로 답을 찾게 하는 방식”이라며 참가자들이 문제 해결을 위한 자신만의 설계를 경험하게 될 것이라고 설명했다.

한일 공동 AI 인재 육성 구상도 제시했다. 최 회장은 기업과 대학의 협력 방안을 묻는 질문에 “한국·일본의 기업과 대학들이 AI 인재를 공동으로 육성하는 프로그램을 만들어 운영하는 것도 좋은 방법”이라고 말했다. 이어 양국의 인턴십과 일자리를 연계해 청년들에게 다양한 기회를 제공하고, 사회 문제 해결에 기여할 혁신가를 양성할 수 있다고 강조했다.

국가마다 문화와 언어, 제도가 다르지만 AI를 활용하는 젊은 세대가 이러한 차이를 극복하며 협력할 수 있다는 것이 최 회장의 판단이다. 앞서 20일 영상 환영사에서도 AI 기술의 발전 방향을 결정하는 인간의 역할과 교육의 중요성을 강조했다.

최 회장은 “AI로 어떤 문제를 해결하고, 어떤 새로운 가치를 창출하며, 어떤 사회를 만들고 싶은지 스스로 물어야 한다”며 AI가 창출한 가치가 사회 전반에 폭넓게 공유되도록 변화를 이끌 인재를 육성해야 한다고 밝혔다. 대학의 역할에 대해서는 “지식을 가르치는 데서 나아가 지혜를 기르는 데 집중해야 한다”고 주문했다.

21일 토론에는 후지이 데루오 도쿄대 총장이 사회자로 참여했으며, 사와다 준 일본전신전화(NTT)그룹 회장, 염재호 태재대학교 총장, 스기무라 미키 소피아대학교 총장 등이 AI 시대의 인재상과 대학의 역할을 논의했다.

최 회장의 제안은 AI 교육을 특정 기술의 활용 능력을 가르치는 수준에서 벗어나 교육과정과 대학 운영체계, 기업의 채용·인재 육성 방식을 함께 변화시키는 과제로 확장했다는 점에서 주목된다. 특히 한일 기업과 대학이 교육 프로그램을 공동으로 운영하고 실제 산업 현장의 인턴십과 취업 기회를 연결하는 구상이 구체화될 경우, AI 전문인력 양성과 국가 간 산업협력을 연계하는 새로운 모델로 발전할 가능성이 있다.
articles.summary: 최태원 SK그룹 회장은 도쿄포럼 2026에서 AI를 기본 환경으로 받아들이는 사회에 맞춰 대학 교육과 거버넌스를 근본적으로 재설계해야 한다고 강조했다. 한국과 일본의 기업·대학이 AI 인재를 공동 육성하고 인턴십과 일자리를 연계하는 프로그램을 제안했으며, SK의 2년제 비학위 프로젝트 교육 프로그램 아이젠을 사례로 소개했다. 핵심은 도구 사용법이나 지식 전달보다 학생이 문제를 정의하고 해결 시스템을 설계하는 역량을 키우는 데 있다. 한일 공동 프로그램은 제안 단계이므로, 실제 운영 체계와 채용 연계 성과는 아직 확인되지 않았다.

articles.title: HapBO: Harnessed $\alpha$-$\pi$ Bayesian Optimization via Expert Natural Language Priors
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25100v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Bayesian Optimization (BO) can be substantially more sample-efficient when informed by prior knowledge about the problem. In practice, however, such knowledge is often available only in natural language, e.g., expert intuitions or documentation, rather than as the explicit probability distribution landscape that prior-guided BO methods may require. Leveraging it effectively demands both an expressive mapping from language to priors and robustness to information that may be misleading. We propose HapBO (Harnessed $\alpha$-$\pi$ Bayesian Optimization), which elicits beliefs once from a human expert, a large language model (LLM), or both, and deterministically compiles a structured specification into a reusable belief function ($\pi: \mathcal{X} \to[0,1]$), with a rich representation not restricted to a Gaussian family. Building on $\alpha$-$\pi$BO, HapBO applies this belief function through a bounded positive multiplier on any nonnegative acquisition, preserving positive acquisition support and requiring no LLM calls during optimization. We prove that, for the Expected Improvement acquisition function (EI), HapBO preserves the standard simple-regret rate up to a bounded factor, even under adversarial beliefs. We evaluate HapBO on 40 HPOBench tasks, a synthetic suite in 6-15 dimensions and two real-world applications: cortical neurostimulation and constrained solar design. HapBO achieves the lowest aggregate HPOBench regret and strong real-world task performance, with zero in-loop token cost. In real-world applications it improves the optimization outcome even at budgets of 12-20 queries, and at a small fraction of the wall-clock and token costs of other LLM-based methods.
articles.summary: HapBO는 전문가나 LLM이 자연어로 제시한 사전 지식을 구조화된 신념 함수로 변환해 베이지안 최적화에 활용한다. 초기 지식 수집 이후에는 최적화 루프에서 LLM을 호출하지 않고, 획득 함수에 제한된 양의 승수를 적용해 잘못된 사전 지식의 영향을 제어한다. 연구진은 Expected Improvement 조건에서 표준 단순 후회율을 유계 계수 범위로 유지함을 증명하고, 40개 HPOBench 과제 및 신경자극·태양광 설계 응용에서 개선을 보고했다. 실험 횟수가 12~20회로 제한된 실제 응용에서도 효과를 보여, 비용이 큰 실험 최적화에 언어 기반 지식을 저렴하게 반영할 가능성이 있다.

articles.title: Auditing Learned Dynamics in Weather Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25119v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Learned weather models are experimentally accessible computational systems whose internal representations can be inspected and manipulated. Using sparse autoencoder features from GraphCast, DeepMind's autoregressive weather forecasting model, we test whether causal relevance requires physical semantics, a question that matters for auditing whether AI forecasters used in high-assurance settings rely on reliable mechanisms. We also look at whether physically associated latent directions can be steered to improve extreme-event forecasts, where interventions are applied to the model's internal activations during the rollout. We find that ablating a feature locked to GraphCast's computational mesh increases global geopotential height error despite lacking conventional physical semantics. Second, suppressing convection- and low-level-vorticity-associated features weakens predicted tropical-cyclone deepening (the fall in central pressure during intensification), while amplifying them reduces intensity error, with amplification of convection features through feature scaling achieving a median of 51\% error reduction over seven storms. Together, these results separate interpretable, physical association from causal utility and establish sparse features as experimental coordinates for auditing and intervening on learned weather dynamics.
articles.summary: 연구진은 GraphCast의 희소 오토인코더 특징을 제거하거나 증폭해, 학습된 기상 모델 내부 표현의 인과적 역할을 조사했다. 전통적인 물리 의미가 뚜렷하지 않은 계산 격자 관련 특징도 제거하면 오차가 늘어, 해석하기 쉬운 특징과 예측에 중요한 특징이 반드시 같지는 않음을 보였다. 대류 관련 특징을 증폭한 실험에서는 열대저기압 7개에 대한 강도 오차 감소율의 중앙값이 51%였다. 내부 활성값 개입이 극한기상 예측 감사와 개선 수단이 될 가능성을 보여주지만, 제한된 폭풍 사례의 결과를 운영 예보 전반에 적용하려면 추가 검증이 필요하다.

articles.title: A Model of Diverse Sampling from Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25003v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models often produce high-quality individual samples but poor sets, with repeated samples clustering around the same semantic modes. We formalize diverse generation as sampling a size-$K$ subset of complete strings from a determinantal point process (DPP), where the likelihood encodes item quality, and the embedding geometry encodes repulsion between similar outputs. Exact inference over all strings is intractable, so we propose PoolDPP: draw a finite candidate pool from a tractable proposal, importance-weight the candidates toward the target quality, and run a $K$-DPP sampler on the induced pool kernel; a greedy MAP variant provides deterministic selection. We prove a finite-sample bound with an explicit constant: the KL divergence between the sampler's output and the target $K$-DPP decays as O(1/N) in the pool size. Empirically, PoolDPP extends the quality--diversity frontier on open-ended generation and the precision--recall frontier on ambiguous text-to-SQL (Ambrosia), and on mathematical reasoning (GSM8K), it raises diversity at about the same pass@$K$.
articles.summary: PoolDPP는 언어모델이 여러 답을 생성할 때 비슷한 의미의 출력에 몰리는 문제를 행렬식 점 과정 기반 집합 샘플링으로 다룬다. 유한 후보군을 생성한 뒤 품질을 중요도 가중치로 반영하고, 임베딩상 유사한 답 사이에 반발을 적용해 K개 출력을 선택한다. 후보 수 N이 늘어날 때 목표 분포와의 KL 발산이 O(1/N)으로 감소하는 경계를 제시했으며, 개방형 생성과 모호한 text-to-SQL에서 품질·다양성 절충을 개선했다. GSM8K에서는 pass@K를 대체로 유지하며 다양성을 높여, 여러 대안을 제시하거나 후속 검증할 답안 집합을 만드는 데 활용할 수 있다.

articles.title: {\phi}TD: Distributional Reinforcement Learning using Characteristic Functions
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25208v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Distributional Reinforcement Learning methods aim to learn the entire distribution of returns, yet current algorithmic approaches are limited to a narrow class of distributions. We propose $\varphi$TD, a method to overcome this limitation by computing the loss in the frequency domain. We demonstrate that this further unifies quantile and categorical approaches to distributional RL, and enables the learning of distributions that were previously impossible to capture, such as mixtures of continuous distributions. We empirically study $\varphi$TD, across synthetic benchmarks and large-scale deep RL environments and demonstrate that the flexibility obtained from wider parametric families can lead to improved performance.
articles.summary: φTD는 기대 보상만이 아니라 수익의 전체 분포를 학습하는 분포적 강화학습에서, 특성함수를 이용해 주파수 영역의 손실을 계산하는 방법이다. 기존 분위수·범주형 접근을 통합하는 관점을 제공하고, 연속 분포의 혼합 등 더 넓은 분포족을 학습할 수 있도록 설계됐다. 합성 벤치마크와 대규모 심층 강화학습 환경에서 이러한 유연성이 성능 향상으로 이어질 수 있다고 보고했다. 제공된 초록에는 환경별 수치가 없어 개선 폭은 판단하기 어렵지만, 복잡한 수익 분포를 표현하는 알고리즘의 선택지를 넓힌다는 의미가 있다.

articles.title: Fast and Memory-Light Evaluation of Density-Based Clusterings with the DISCO Index in R
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25114v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: DISCO is a recent internal cluster validity index for density-based clustering that, unlike earlier indices, also evaluates the quality of noise labels. The discoCVI package makes DISCO available in R. This article describes the design of the package and a typical workflow, in which DISCO is used to compare clusterings and to choose the parameters of HDBSCAN without ground truth, followed by the implementation introduced in version 0.2.0. DISCO is defined through density-connectivity distances between all pairs of points, so direct implementations store several n-by-n matrices. We show that every quantity DISCO needs can be read off the single-linkage merge tree of the mutual-reachability minimum spanning tree, so that the index can be computed exactly with memory that grows linearly with the number of points, while the running time remains quadratic as in the original definition. The implementation is tested against the previous version, agrees with the original Python implementation to within $3 \times 10^{-13}$, and corrects the score of singleton clusters to match the published definition. In benchmarks, discoCVI is 23 to 138 times faster than its previous version for 500 to 4,000 points and 3 to 9 times faster than the Python reference for 500 to 8,000 points, using a fraction of the memory of both, and it scores 100,000 points in about 50 seconds with less than 200 MB of memory.
articles.summary: R 패키지 discoCVI 0.2.0은 잡음 라벨의 품질까지 평가하는 밀도 기반 군집 검증 지수 DISCO를 선형 메모리로 정확하게 계산하도록 구현을 개선했다. 상호 도달 가능성 최소 신장 트리의 단일 연결 병합 트리에서 필요한 값을 추출해 여러 개의 제곱 크기 행렬을 저장하지 않으며, 시간 복잡도는 기존과 같은 이차 수준이다. 벤치마크에서 이전 버전보다 23~138배, Python 참조 구현보다 3~9배 빨랐고, 10만 개 점을 200MB 미만 메모리로 약 50초에 평가했다. 정답 라벨 없이 HDBSCAN 매개변수를 비교하는 실무의 메모리 부담을 줄이며, 단일 원소 군집의 점수도 발표된 정의에 맞게 수정했다.
